timeline.reflection: From 11:00 Marcus was on shop equipment repair at moderate to very heavy effort, and his body heated up about 0.06 °C faster every half hour than the plan expected. This happened over 2 slots. He is acclimatized and no alerts fired, so this was not a safety breakdown. The problem is that the plan treated shop repair as easier on the body than it really is in late-morning heat, and stacked the heavy and very heavy parts of the job back to back at the hottest part of his shift. The plan underestimated the heat load of this task, which also cut how much got done (throughput 0.70).

op.text: Treat shop equipment repair as harder work than its label once the day warms up. Lifting, awkward positions and indoor heat build-up wear a worker down faster than planned.
Schedule the heaviest repair work, like lifting, teardown and reassembly, before 11:00. Save diagnostics and paperwork for late morning and midday.
After 11:00, don't stack heavy and very heavy repair slots back to back for one person. Put a light or moderate task between them, even for acclimatized workers.

His body temperature climbed about 0.13 °C faster every 30 minutes than the plan expected, for three slots in a row. No alert fired, but the margin was eaten up quickly. That forced a conservative pace, which is likely why throughput (0.63) and the overall score (0.42) came out low.
